_readme: Cross-platform phone conformance corpus (D-288). The authentication surface parses phone numbers on
three platforms with three INDEPENDENT libphonenumber ports: libphonenumber-csharp (backend),
libphonenumber-js (web + admin) and phone_numbers_parser (Flutter). Their version numbers are not
comparable to each other, so there is nothing to pin — the only thing that can be held stable is
BEHAVIOUR. Each platform has a test that reads this file and asserts it produces exactly these
results, so a metadata drift that would make one platform reject what another accepts fails CI
instead of failing a user who cannot register.
Adding a case: pick a number that is real-shaped but not a real subscriber, and add it here first.
If a platform then fails, that platform's metadata is the outlier — bump it, do not edit the

cases.note: Singapore — 10-digit E.164, corrupted by the old length rule
Norway — 10-digit E.164, corrupted by the old length rule
Denmark — 10-digit E.164, corrupted by the old length rule
Germany — 13 digits, the long end of the range
Unassigned country code — must never be given an invented country
Too short to be anyone's number
Parses AND resolves to SG, but is not a real Singapore range — parseable is not valid, which is the distinction every platform must agree on
